records.whole_exchange_context: Manuel Almeida politely asks Admiral Lil Argot for a moment. She casually invites him to explain. He personally found an interesting paper fragment at the library in Alexandria the other day. Her question prompts his account of its contents: a mysterious chisel said to have been used by Phidias, the legendary sculptor of ancient Greece, in creating his works. She clarifies the practical tool: a cutting implement used with a hammer to carve wood or stone. He recounts beliefs that the sculptor's soul passed into the chisel after his death and that its user would show miraculous talent for shaping or sculpture. These remain reported beliefs, not narrator-confirmed supernatural powers or repair statistics. The paper offers only a reported burial somewhere on the Balkan Peninsula near Greece and gives no precise location. Lil familiarly addresses Manuel and teasingly asks if he wants it for repairing ships. He breezily defends the idea with a reported Roman kings-as-tools policy comparison, finding kings rather lavish tools. Preserve the repeated tools metaphor and its humor. He then calls ships works of art, defends fine tools for making them, and makes a gentle request to search if an opportunity arises.
